newsitem.title: USA: US spot resid prices unchanged to down with crude.
newsitem.headline: US spot resid prices unchanged to down with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to off slightly again Tuesday in sluggish trade, with further losses in crude and a lack of utility demand still undermining sentiment, industry sources said.

"Without any (cold) weather surprises, resid could stay under pressure for the next week or two," said one cash trader, adding there were still several unsold pieces of high and low sulphur looking for a home.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to $19.25-50 a barrel, with November and December paper quoted modestly lower with crude at $19.55 and $20.10, respectively.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally slipped slightly to about $21.25, with some talking the grade even lower.
High sulphurs in NYH held relatively steady, with 2.2 percent still seen at $18.50-75.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was stable at about $18.25, while three percent lost a quarter to $16.25-50, traders said.
USG November three percent paper sold at $16.75, with sellers now at $17.
New York City gate swing gas tumbled at least 15 cents Tuesday to about the $2.90/mmBtu level on mild weather in the area. NYH one percent resid was at a $3.08/mmBtu equivalent.
